title: Governor Braun announces second year of statewide tuition freeze at Indiana public colleges
text:
Governor Braun announces second year of statewide tuition freeze at Indiana public colleges
Governor Mike Braun announced on Aug. 26 that Indiana's statewide tuition freeze for in-state undergraduate students will continue for a second consecutive academic year, affecting all 15 of the state's public colleges and universities.
The tuition and mandatory fee freeze, which began in the 2025-26 academic year at Governor Braun’s request, will extend through the 2026-27 academic year. The measure applies to both main and regional campuses across institutions such as Ball State University, Indiana State University, Ivy Tech Community College, Purdue University campuses, University of Southern Indiana, Vincennes University, and all Indiana University locations.
"Hoosier students are returning to campus with tuition frozen at every public college and university in Indiana for the second year. Indiana’s public institutions answered my call to find efficiencies and put students and their families first. In Indiana, your higher education dollar stretches further," Governor Mike Braun said.
Braun called on higher education institutions to identify efficiencies by eliminating redundancies and streamlining services without compromising educational quality. All 15 institutions agreed to maintain a zero percent increase in tuition and mandatory fees for two years. The initiative was unanimously endorsed by the Indiana Commission for Higher Education. This marks the first time every public higher education institution in the state has held tuition flat simultaneously over two consecutive years.
Braun contributed to public service through roles on school boards and in state representation; achieved growth of his company into a national entity employing thousands; championed over 40 bills that became law during his Senate term; has been married for 49 years with four children; won election to the U.S. Senate in 2018 before becoming governor; and graduated summa cum laude with a degree in economics from Wabash College before earning an MBA from Harvard Business School, according to the official website.
